## The defect

`CodeHealthConfig.enabled` (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:538`, default `False`) has ZERO read
sites in `src/rebar`. Nothing gates on it.

A code trace of the live path confirms it: `_commands/metrics.py:139-148` loads
`config.load_config(root).code_health` and carries only `scan_roots` (:144), `size_cap` (:145) and
`size_near_fraction` (:146) into the metrics context. `enabled` is never consulted, so the
structural metrics (`module_size_distribution`, `oversized_module_count`, `complexity_summary`,
`duplication_summary`) evaluate even at the default `enabled=False`.

The field is documented and settable, so an operator can set `enabled = false` and reasonably
believe code-health analysis is off. It is not.

## Why it was never caught

The 6754 inert-config gate cannot see this one -- see the sibling bug on that gate. It matches
bare attribute NAMES globally, and `.enabled` is read on other configs (`ui.enabled`,
`LangfuseConfig`, under `llm/`), so this field passes without ever being read itself. That is also
why it carries no `# read-via:` marker while the neighbouring `analyzers` field needed one.

## The decision this needs

Same shape as dce2: either HONOR the flag (gate structural metric evaluation on it) or DELETE it.
Honoring it is a behavioral change -- metrics that run today would stop running for anyone on the
default -- so this needs an explicit operator ruling, not an agent's judgment.

Note the interaction with dce2's ruling: the operator chose to DELETE the inert `analyzers` field
rather than wire it, with intent preserved as idea 94bc-a0b4-bc37-47b2. A consistent ruling here
is plausible but must not be assumed, because the two differ -- deleting `analyzers` removes a knob
that never did anything, whereas deleting `enabled` removes the only advertised off switch for the
whole code-health subsystem.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An explicit operator decision is recorded: honor `enabled` or remove it.
- [ ] If HONORED: structural metric evaluation is gated on it, with a test proving the metrics do
      NOT evaluate at `enabled=False` and DO at `enabled=True`; the default's behavior change is
      called out in the changelog.
- [ ] If REMOVED: the field, its coercion row and its config-surface entries go, and the docs no
      longer advertise an off switch that does not exist.
- [ ] Either way, a guard prevents it silently regressing to inert again (this depends on the 6754
      gate fix -- a same-named field cannot be policed until that lands).

## Provenance

Found by a code-trace archaeology pass over the metrics/code-health system while scoping dce2.

## Fix plan (REMOVAL, per the operator ruling above)

Pure removal — the field controls nothing today, so deleting it cannot change what runs.

1. `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — delete the `enabled: bool = False` field from
   `CodeHealthConfig`, delete its `"enabled": lambda v, k: _as_bool(v, k)` coercion row from
   the `code_health` entry of `_SECTIONS`, and refresh the class docstring (it no longer
   describes an inert-by-default toggle).
2. `src/rebar/_deprecations.py` — add TWO warn-class tombstones so a still-set key WARNs and
   exits 0 rather than being silently dropped: an `env` tombstone for
   `REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED` and a `cfg` tombstone for `code_health.enabled`. This is
   mandatory, not optional: `tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py` fails the build when a
   golden-pinned key exists in neither the live schema nor the tombstone registry.
3. `docs/config.md` — drop `enabled` from both TOML examples and from the prose type list in
   the `code_health.*` section, and add both tombstoned inputs to the warn-class list.
4. `tests/unit/test_code_health_config.py` and `tests/unit/test_code_health_config_heldout.py`
   — drop the `enabled` assertions, the `-c code_health.enabled=true` CLI override, and the
   `code_health.enabled` / `REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED` golden-surface expectations.
5. `tests/scripts/test_metrics_docs.py` — drop `enabled` from the documented-keys tuple.

Not touched: `tests/golden/config_surface.json` stays pinned (that is the point of the golden —
the tombstones account for the removed entries).

`_as_bool` is NOT orphaned by this removal (dozens of other coercion rows use it), unlike
dce2's `_as_str_dict`.

### Evidence of no behavior change

`rebar metrics` before and after produce the same structural metrics. A byte-identical diff is
not achievable — two consecutive runs already differ in time- and store-driven ticket metrics
(dce2 found the same) — so the evidence is per-metric attribution over the code_health lens.

### On the guard AC

MOOT for a deleted field: there is nothing left to regress to inert. It also depended on bug
2c58-e710-275e-4ff7 regardless — the current inert-config gate could never have caught this
field, because `.enabled` is read on other configs.
